A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Streaming-VR research despite the changed title. All 14 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison. The original case study moves from Appendix D to E.

before.justification: v3 reports original ASQA and QuoteSum evaluations, verifier accuracy, model-component comparisons, latency measurements, and error analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, verifier accuracy, latency measurements, and error analyses.

M1.justification: The sentence-level verification/refinement procedure, verifier training, and contextual refinement remain unchanged. Section 3.2 adds a tilde to the verifier's preceding-answer argument, aligning its formula with the existing description of updated preceding sentences; this does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use ASQA and QuoteSum with the same closed/open-book and zero/few-shot coverage, including varying retrieved-passage and example counts. The added memory discussion introduces no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Full-VR, unrefined backbone models, Self-VR and verifier/refiner variants, the Random verifier, and Self-RAG 7B/13B. The revised Table 5 caption names the already evaluated Self-RAG baseline.

E3.justification: New Appendix D adds maximum GPU memory as a resource-comparison measure for LLaMA-3.1 8B generation and Mistral 7B verification, without specifying a measurement protocol. Existing benchmark splits, retrieval settings, quality metrics, training settings, and latency procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a limited analysis of whether Streaming-VR requires more peak GPU memory than Full-VR. Existing passage/shot sensitivity analyses, verifier/refiner comparisons, derailed-answer analysis, and the relocated case study are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same error-bar reporting. Neither version supplies additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v5 newly reports approximately 43,900 MB of GPU memory, expressed as 16,035 + 27,865 MB, and states that both methods have the same maximum usage. Tables 1–5, plotted benchmark results, and the 3.07-second versus 5.98-second latency results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the verifier argument to use the refined prefix. Appendix C changes N = 7 to N = 4 in the latency argument while still saying 'seven sentences,' introducing an internal inconsistency. The latency formulas and inequality chain otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the central claims about intermediate correction, error propagation, and efficiency with comparable answer quality remain intact. v5's introduction highlights the 1.95× speedup already reported in v3.

C2.justification: New Appendix D argues that equal maximum token loads imply equal peak GPU-memory requirements, adding a deployment interpretation. Existing explanations of over-correction, verifier/refiner capabilities, error propagation, and synthetic-label limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a model-specific GPU-memory footprint and revises the open-model access description from HuggingFace API to HuggingFace Hub. The verifier's five epochs, 1e-5 learning rate, AdamW optimizer, and augmentation temperatures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged. Positioning relative to retrieval augmentation, verification, iterative refinement, and intrinsic self-correction retains the same substance.

P1.justification: v5 changes the title to 'Efficient Real-time Refinement of Language Model Text Generation,' updates author contacts, adds acknowledgments, and makes local grammar and terminology edits. The main narrative structure remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is recolored and its correction arrow relabeled 'Update the Sentence'; the augmentation prompt box is redesigned. Existing figures and tables are resized or relocated, including separating Table 1 and Figures 2–3 across pages, while their basic structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: v5 improves presentation and resource documentation through clearer notation, the redesigned prompt display, and GPU-memory information. However, Appendix C introduces the unresolved 'seven sentences (N = 4)' contradiction into the latency argument, and the memory claim lacks a stated measurement protocol. With the benchmark evidence unchanged, these limited gains and weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
